title: AI makes junior lawyers look better on paper, and that makes it harder to tell whether they are learning
discussion_signal: The post emphasizes the gap between assisted output and durable expertise. It reports better AI-assisted patent drafts, but says unaided gains were concentrated among senior lawyers while junior outcomes diverged. The discussion turns this into an apprenticeship question: firms may need to assess judgment separately from tool-produced work.
linked_research_question: In industrial knowledge work, when does AI assistance build judgment and when does it conceal missing apprenticeship, and how should firms measure worker capability without the tool?
limits: The discussion is a selected interpretation of a short field experiment
The experiment concerns patent lawyers and may not generalize to other occupations
Public reactions are not a representative sample of workers or employers
